clips.title: He grew more in 2 months than in 4 years of college
clips.speaker: Ohaji
clips.hook_q: How did 2 months beat 4 years of college?
clips.hook_plain: Did school teach you to fear failure?
clips.transcript: I've grown more in these last two months I was in the internship than I have in four years in college. This is insane. I've learned more about how real life works and about failure, and you get taught during school, failure is bad. If you get that F, it's bad. You want to aim for the A. But what you learn and what I learned from the internship is you fail, you keep going. You fail, you get back up. Failure is good. Failure is a chance to learn, and that is life.

clips.title: Stop sending 'I'll do your marketing' DMs
clips.speaker: Andrew + Blake
clips.hook_q: Why your cold DMs aren't working?
clips.transcript: We all get DMs all the time where it's like, hey, I will make you YouTube thumbnails or I will do your marketing task or I'll do your GHL stuff, whatever it may be. And they don't leave with listening. Actually, what are the pain points that they're having? So I would say if you're new and starting an agency, you're trying to get your first few customers, that's an absolutely huge deal. A huge deal. Yeah, because that allows you to go for first. Take your time and just listen.

clips.title: Posting at 10 years old killed her fear of judgement
clips.speaker: McKinley
clips.hook_q: How do you stop caring what people think?
clips.hook_plain: She started posting at 10 years old
clips.transcript: I remember the first time I posted a YouTube video, I was like 10 years old. And I knew that in order to make it grow, I had to post it on my other social channels to let people know about it. And that was really, really scary because I knew all my friends with school would talk about it and they did, but it's fun. It was really intimidating and frightening, but now flash forward, it's like, I don't even, every time I post, I don't even think about what other people are thinking because it's just like, okay, I'm gonna post again tomorrow or the next day. And just, it's like a numbers game.

clips.title: Offer one thing. Then find your groove.
clips.speaker: Blake
clips.hook_q: One piece of advice for new agency owners?
clips.transcript: I would say probably don't sit back and wait. If you're on the fence and you really wanna get out there, just start talking to people. I mean, I know you've talked about it, I mean, but get involved, go to events. When I first started, I went to B &I meetings. I went to Chamber of Commerce meetings and just have confidence in yourself. And find one thing that you can offer someone and don't try to do too much. There's so much out there. I think if you can make a great living or you can really get a great start just by starting off offering one thing.

clips.title: Show me your 3 friends, I'll show you your future
clips.speaker: Ohaji
clips.hook_q: Are your friends holding you back?
clips.transcript: Even during the internship, we went through periods this time, me specifically, where it's just hard. It's hard, I was feeling, seeing people get clients, and I'm like, well, where are my clients? I'm doing everything right, supposedly. But one thing that really killed me growing up was obviously the people around me. Your ecosystem, you are who you're around. You show me your three friends, and I'll show you where you're going in life.

clips.title: Forget speed to lead. Speed to support.
clips.speaker: Blake
clips.hook_q: Is slow support killing your agency?
clips.hook_plain: Speed to support > speed to lead
clips.transcript: We actually have a direct ticket system built inside the app as well. So when people are using task engine and they run into something, they can literally click a button, submit a ticket to our team, and then we can turn around and respond to that. And I think it's a big necessity is speed. Everybody talks about speed to lead and speed, but I think about speed to support. I think that when people get caught up, they want an answer quick.
